Let the original apex be \(S\), and let the two marked midpoints be \(M\) and \(N\) on the two base edges meeting at \(A\).

The cut plane contains \(S\), \(M\), and \(N\). The part containing \(A\) is the smaller pyramid with apex \(S\) and base triangle \(AMN\).

If the square base has side length \(s\), then
\[
AM=\frac{s}{2}, \qquad AN=\frac{s}{2},
\]
and \(\angle MAN=90^\circ\). Hence
\[
[AMN]=\frac12\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)
=\frac{s^2}{8}.
\]
The original square base has area \(s^2\), so the new base area is \(\frac18\) of the original base area. The height from \(S\) to the base plane is unchanged.

Therefore, the volume of the part containing \(A\) is
\[
\frac18\cdot 480=60.
\]
